translations.en: 24 – Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Mihran, al-Karkhi, Abu Ja'far. A ghali (exaggerator), weak, a liar. He has a book regarding the praised and the blamed that indicates his filth and his lying.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Duʿafāʾ* critiques Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Karkhī, a prominent but controversial figure in early Shia hadith transmission. His classification as a *ghalī* (exaggerator) and *kadhdhāb* (liar) reflects the rigorous scrutiny applied to narrators whose theological views on the Imams' divinity or authority were deemed excessive or unorthodox by mainstream scholars.
en.seo_question: Who is Muhammad ibn 'Abdallah ibn Mihran al-Karkhi and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.غَالٍ: Ghali: One who exaggerates, particularly regarding the virtues or divinity of the Imams.
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak: A narrator whose reliability or precision is considered low.
key_terms.كَذَّابٌ: Liar: A narrator known for fabricating or frequently making errors.
key_terms.الْمَمْدُوحِينَ وَالْمَذْمُومِينَ: The Praised and the Blamed: Title of his book, indicating a work on evaluating people.
